market_thesis.long_term: The binding constraint on AI is no longer chips but power, permits and local political consent — which structurally advantages regulated utilities, gas, nuclear, copper and grid hardware over fabless narratives, but only after the market finishes repricing who captures (versus who gets taxed on) that electricity. Supply chains keep duplicating: Nvidia policing cloud partners to block Chinese access, China blocking SoftBank-ABB, Europe reselling GPU access at 30-50% premiums — all of which embeds a permanently higher capex baseline and a higher inflation floor. Households spending more on food, housing and insurance entrenches a decade of bifurcation: value retail, generics and distribution, security-type products and healthcare delivery take share from undifferentiated discretionary. Humanoid robotics and agentic software become real capital sinks but, as Agility's IPO shows, the equity will be priced on losses for years.

shifts.shift: Compute and electricity have merged into one asset class; firm power, not GPUs, is the binding constraint on AI, so hyperscaler balance sheets now fund generation directly.

Housing need is satisfied by substitution, not purchase: lock-in at 7%+ converts turnover demand into remodel, rental permanence and multigenerational living; capital is explicitly rotating from dwellings to data centers.
A ~5% risk-free rate and $365tn of global debt are the regime; term premium stays structurally elevated, permanently impairing business models whose moat was cheap capital.

Agent delegation creates a permanent market for identity, permissioning, audit and runtime containment — security becomes a metered utility on every automated action rather than a periodic product purchase.

Energy security displaces energy transition as the organizing political and consumer need; infrastructure becomes a military target, converting resilience from cyclical capex into policy-mandated spend.

Consumer spending bifurcates by income rather than shrinking: value retail and experiences at the extremes win, mid-tier branded goods and the mid-market experience economy lose wallet share, and the bottom half funds the same basket with credit.

Consumers buy AI as reclaimed time, not as intelligence — delegation of low-status obligations (phone calls, scheduling, shopping) is the primary consumer use case, and it migrates to the edge for cost, latency and privacy.

Health demand shifts from episodic treatment to purchased healthspan — less-invasive procedures, devices, continuous monitoring and early detection — driven by an aging, shrinking population actively shopping interventions.

Western demographic contraction from ~2029 makes productivity-per-worker the only growth lever and keeps skilled physical trades (electricians, HVAC, pipeline, fab construction) structurally scarce and well paid.

Market structure unbundles along time, access and venue simultaneously — 24/7 and tokenized trading, retail private-market access, new exchanges — shifting economics to venues, brokers and rails and away from asset gatherers.
